task.title: Show a board edit that origin overrode on a task this clone compacted
task.description:
Found in review of PR #215 (2026-11-21), not a regression from it.

When this clone compacts a task by hand and then edits its description, and origin's older copy of the task also edits the description, the next sync replays origin's history onto the local checkpoint and origin's text wins. The old tip is parked, but the new tip descends from it, so the board treats the parked edit as already carried and shows no set-aside notice. The text survives in the task's history only, and the parked ref can later be retired.

Reproduced by the reviewer: description becomes "Their text", one parked ref, nothing shown as set aside. Cause: a parked tip that is already in the task's history counts as settled (internal/gitstore/setaside.go, near the ancestry check). Suggested fix: compare against the replayed commits rather than ancestry alone.

Also from the same review, smaller:
- Titles, labels and link labels still draw the invisible fillers U+3164 and U+115F, and prose blocks keep a raw ESC, on the whole board and not only in the set-aside notice.
- The server's log line for an unreadable parked ref repeats each time the task's tip moves, and the record of lines already logged never shrinks.

## Done when
- An edit overridden this way is shown as set aside until someone deals with it or dismisses it, with a test using temporary repositories.
